why: RBF, Matern, and the other stationary kernels build every training covariance through the symmetric (X2 is None) path. On 2000 by 8 inputs that path spends most of its time in tdot, which is much slower than a GEMM at this shape, then np.clip copies the full matrix. An np.dot plus an in-place square root matched within 2e-15 and was 3.8x faster on the same draws (median about 22 ms versus 84 ms). The call-to-call spread is large because the routine is memory-bound on one core, and it is still well under that speedup.

Expectation propagation calls this with quad_mode='gh' on every likelihood-parameter step for Student-T, Gamma, and any other likelihood that does not override it. It maps a 32-point Gauss-Hermite integral, including a Python elementwise product, across observations. Applying the same nodes to all 800 rows at once matched the scalar result to about 4e-15 and cut the median from 30 ms to about 0.5 ms.

Diagonal Student-T prediction (GP.predict, full_cov=False) ends here. For nu>2 and the identity link the observation variance is Var(f) + sigma^2 * nu / (nu - 2), which test_likelihood already checks at rtol 1e-6, but the method still runs three scipy.quad integrations per test point. On 32 points the quadrature result is within 2e-9 of that closed form, so almost all of the 22 ms is avoidable.
